newsitem.title: USA: Los Angeles transit agency adopts code of conduct.
newsitem.headline: Los Angeles transit agency adopts code of conduct.

text.p: The Los Angeles Metropolitan Transportation Authority's board of directors voted on Friday to adopt a new code of conduct for board members, alternates, and their staff, the authority said.

The new code will revise the transportation authority's existing ethics policy to tighten gift and political contribution rules, and would restrict contact between board members and staff in the awarding of contracts.
Metropolitan Transportation Authority Chairman Larry Zarian said the purpose of the new ethics policy was to "eliminate even the appearance of impropriety."

Under the new code, board members are prohibited from accepting gifts totaling $289 or more from a single source in a calendar year, and cannot accept or solicit gifts from contractors, potential contractors or subcontractors.
The new code seeks to separate board involvement from the day-to-day work of the staff, the hiring of staff, and the hiring of employees by contractors or subcontractors.
The code of conduct also "spells out the need for courteous communication" between board members, and between board members and staff, the authority said.
Officials who violate the policy could face public censure by the board, disqualification from voting, suspension from the board, or a fine, the authority said.

"The new code lays out comprehensive guidelines for Board members, and it assures the public that everyone on the Board is fully committed to maintaining the absolute integrity of government," Zarian said.
In recent weeks, the Los Angeles transportation authority has come under increasing fire from state and federal officials over planning, funding and management changes.

In a January 6 letter to the authority, Federal Transit Administrator Gordon Linton expressed concerns about the agency's ability to manage its projects in the face of cost overruns and a projected $1 billion hole in the county's long-range transportation plan.
